name: Al-Baitul Amien Mosque
summary:
Al-Baitul Amien Grand Mosque (Indonesian: Masjid Agung Al-Baitul Amien) in Jember, East Java, Indonesia, is one of East Java's significant regional mosques, serving the Muslim community of Jember — a major agricultural town in East Java known for tobacco cultivation — and reflecting the deep integration of Islamic practice into Javanese and Indonesian social and cultural life. The mosque represents the local expression of Indonesian Islamic architecture that blends Middle Eastern influences with Javanese cultural elements.

Indonesia is the world's most populous Muslim-majority country (approximately 270 million population, approximately 87% Muslim), and Java — with approximately 150 million people — is the world's most populous island and home to the majority of Indonesian Muslims. East Java is historically significant for Islam: the Wali Songo (Nine Saints, Islamic missionaries who spread Islam in Java in the 15th-16th centuries) had significant presence in East Java, and the region developed a distinctive Javanese Islam that synthesized Islamic practice with pre-Islamic Javanese culture.

Jember's Al-Baitul Amien mosque, as a major city mosque in East Java, serves the community functions that mosques play in Indonesian Islamic life: not only daily prayers and Friday sermons but Islamic education, social welfare programs, and community organization. The mosque's architecture — combining dome and minaret elements with local Javanese architectural traditions — reflects the visual synthesis that characterizes Indonesian mosque design.
